newsitem.title: UK: North Sea mixed as Dated firms, grades slip back.
newsitem.headline: North Sea mixed as Dated firms, grades slip back.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mixed on Thursday as Dated Brent firmed and other grades eased under the weight of an overhang of late April barrels, traders said.

Despite claims by some producers that differentials were broadly unchanged from Wednesday, when values edged higher on improved refining margins and the sight of cargoes moving to the U.S., traders said Forties and Statfjord had slipped back.

Dated Brent, however, was talked in a wide range of May Brent -70/-50 cents after an early April/May spread deal at -40 cents which valued the benchmark grade at June Brent -65 cents, broadly in line with next week's CFDs.
"The early Brents may move for (May) -75 and the later ones for around -40," said a trader.
Brent intermonth spreads lost ground, May/June trading at -23 and -24 cents, about 12 cents below Wednesday's higher levels, while June/July also lost about 10 cents to talk at -16/-13 cents.
Brent CFDs shed a similar amount as April 14-18 dates changed hands at June Brent -64 and -66.50 cents.
Two Brent cargoes nominated April 25-27 loading dates were kept by J.P. Morgan and BP, dealers said. Other North Sea grades were suffering, however, from unsold April stems.

An April 25-27 Forties cargo traded at Dated Brent +6 cent, four cents weaker than on Wednesday and there was unconfirmed talk of a late month cargo of Statfjord changing hands at Dated Brent +7/+8 cents, two or three cents weaker than the previous reported deal.
"Statfjord will go lower than (Dated) +10 cents. There are still a few cargoes left in the last decade, along with a couple of Ekofisks," said a trader.
The first of the May North Sea loading programmes are expected to be released on Friday, traders said.
